speaker: interviewer
text: Hi Omar, thanks for joining. Is now a good time?

speaker: interviewee
text: Yes, yes, I'm in the car, parked. I have twenty minutes before I collect my son.

speaker: interviewer
text: Perfect. So this is just about your grocery orders, no wrong answers.

speaker: interviewee
text: Okay, go ahead.

speaker: interviewer
text: Great. Tell me a bit about your household and who does the food shopping.

speaker: interviewee
text: We are me, my wife Leila, our son, he's eight, and Leila's mother lives with us. Leila's mother runs the kitchen, honestly. I drive her to the shops on Friday, the butcher and the big supermarket next to it.

speaker: interviewer
text: Great, great. And how did you hear about Shmuber Eats?

speaker: interviewee
text: An advert, on my phone, while I was reading the news.

speaker: interviewer
text: Great. Walk me through your last Shmuber Eats order, from opening the app to putting things away.

speaker: interviewee
text: So, Leila's cousins rang at four in the afternoon to say they were driving up from the coast and would be with us for dinner, all six of them, and there was no time to go out and also cook. So Leila's mother dictated, and I typed. Lamb, rice, aubergines, yogurt, herbs, bread, fruit, a lot of everything. Friday mornings with her mother at the butcher is still how we do it, that was a one-time rescue.

speaker: interviewer
text: Great. Let's move on. How often do you order groceries online?

speaker: interviewee
text: That was the first time. Maybe once since, for water.

speaker: interviewer
text: And the order for water, how did that go?

speaker: interviewee
text: Easy. Twelve big bottles, and the driver carried them in. My back thanked him.

speaker: interviewer
text: Great. Tell me about the last time an item in your order was substituted.

speaker: interviewee
text: The herbs. We asked for fresh coriander and got parsley. Leila's mother noticed immediately, of course. But she fixed it, she always has something in the garden.

speaker: interviewer
text: Did you know about it before the delivery arrived?

speaker: interviewee
text: No, I only knew when she started shouting at the bag. Haha. I think there was a message, but I was cleaning the house.

speaker: interviewer
text: Haha. Great. How do you keep track of what you need between orders?

speaker: interviewee
text: Leila's mother keeps it in her head. She is the list. Leila writes some things on her phone for the pharmacy.

speaker: interviewer
text: Haha. Does Leila ever add things to an order?

speaker: interviewee
text: She sends me a photo of the empty box. That's her list.

speaker: interviewer
text: Great. How did you pick the delivery window last time?

speaker: interviewee
text: It was the six to eight that evening, the last one that day. It came at six forty, which was fine.

speaker: interviewer
text: And on a normal day, would a two-hour slot work for you?

speaker: interviewee
text: Somebody is always home, so yes. That's not a problem for us.

speaker: interviewer
text: Great, great. What would you think of a monthly delivery pass, and what would you pay for it?

speaker: interviewee
text: For us, no. We don't order enough. Maybe if it was two, three a month.

speaker: interviewer
text: What about 9.99 a month, with free delivery?

speaker: interviewee
text: No, no. Leila's mother would never agree. She likes to see the meat.

speaker: interviewer
text: Haha. Great. What did you like most about it?

speaker: interviewee
text: That it was fast. I ordered, and two hours later it was at the door.

speaker: interviewer
text: And what did you like least?

speaker: interviewee
text: The coriander. And the app showed me a lot of offers before I could search.

speaker: interviewer
text: Noted, offers. Great. Did you pay with a card in the app?

speaker: interviewee
text: Yes, my card. It was quick.

speaker: interviewer
text: Noted. Great. On a scale of one to ten, how was it overall?

speaker: interviewee
text: Eight. It was quick and easy.

speaker: interviewer
text: Great. Did anyone else in the family use the app?

speaker: interviewee
text: No, only me. Leila's mother doesn't trust it. She trusts me with the phone.

speaker: interviewer
text: Haha. Great. Last question, is there anything about your orders I didn't ask about?

speaker: interviewee
text: No, I think that's it. I have to go get my son soon.

speaker: interviewer
text: Of course. Thank you so much, Omar, this was really helpful.

speaker: interviewee
text: You're welcome. Goodbye.
